accepted_blueprint_role.advances_plan: Marchesa converts the deck's interaction into card selection and graveyard setup.
accepted_blueprint_role.honest_note: All three win packages work without her, and the list is the exact copy of a tournament-winning list (Takeda Ryuhei, 2026-10-11), a 48-card rebuild from the source baseline (decisions L10, L12). She is a selection engine in a generic Grixis cEDH shell, not a kill. The cycle 51 M1 review (marchdod-01..08, all verified) confirms the crime rules and the three wins.

authority.note: Structural commander-reference counts are a counterfactual prior only; they cannot decide deck changes or commander value.

counterfactual_questions: Which declared wins disappear or change when the commander is unavailable?
Which declared engines/packages explicitly require the commander?
Which Spellbook lines remain structurally independent?
How much dynamic card economy, action efficiency, assembly speed and recovery actually changes? (deferred to later Step D batches)
limitations: Exact-name/Blueprint support is structural evidence, not a complete rules-interaction detector.
A route without an explicit commander reference may still gain substantial value from the commander in play.
A route with an explicit commander reference may have redundant alternate routes not captured by a single Blueprint field.
Counts are intentionally not combined into a synthetic commander-value score.
Dynamic effects on cards drawn, meaningful actions, mana spent, combo timing and recovery require the Step D counterfactual simulator layer.
